title: Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd - 544780 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Vedanta Aluminium Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR21,105 crore (+45% YoY) and EBITDA INR10,499 crore (+134% YoY) on higher realisations.
summary.overview: This was a combined Q1 FY27 call for five demerged Vedanta entities, with Vedanta Aluminium (VAML) the standout: record aluminium output of 632 kt, record revenue and EBITDA, and EBITDA per ton up to USD1,804 from USD1,511 quarter-on-quarter. Hot metal cost fell 3% QoQ to USD1,698/t and full-year guidance of USD1,650–1,700/t is unchanged, with Q2 slightly higher on monsoon power-plant shutdowns. Management guided FY27 alumina output of 4–4.1 mt with a back-half-weighted profile, and set out a dividend framework of 4–5% yield on each entity's market capitalisation. Vedanta Power's Q1 was hit by a Sakti boiler incident, with Unit 1 restart now guided for end-September or early October.

financial_highlights.change: includes INR1,097 crore discontinued ops gain; continuing PAT -INR151 crore

segments.name: Vedanta Aluminium (VAML)
segments.commentary: Record aluminium production of 632 kt (+5% YoY, +3% QoQ) and sales of 615 kt; alumina output 826 kt (+41% YoY, -6% QoQ); value-added products a record 389 kt (+14% YoY).

segments.name: Vedanta Oil & Gas
segments.commentary: Gross operated production 77.7 kboe/d (Rajasthan 63.1, offshore 11.6, OALP 3.1); unit opex USD17.4/bbl (-3% QoQ); FY27 direct opex guided in line with FY26; EBITDA flat YoY.

segments.name: Vedanta Power
segments.commentary: Sales 5,224 MU (+38% YoY); Meenakshi record quarterly EBITDA INR112 crore; Talwandi Sabo availability 86% from 77% QoQ; Sakti Unit 1 restart guided for end-Sep/early-Oct.

segments.name: Vedanta Iron & Steel
segments.commentary: Sellable steel 582 kt with 12% steel EBITDA margin; iron ore production 2.6 mt (+4% YoY); net debt INR2,733 crore post demerger adjustments, net debt/EBITDA 1.3x.

segments.name: Vedanta Limited (zinc, copper, etc.)
segments.commentary: Zinc India refined metal 260 kt (+4% YoY) at lowest-ever cost of USD851/t; Gamsberg cost USD1,549/t; FACOR best-ever EBITDA INR101 crore; Copper India sales 53 kt (+3% YoY).

guidance_outlook: VAML FY27 hot metal cost guidance unchanged at USD1,650–1,700/t; Q2 may be marginally higher due to monsoon power-plant shutdowns; management expects USD175–200/t reduction over 3–4 quarters from Lanjigarh ramp, Sijimali and Ghogharpalli.
VAML alumina production FY27 guided at 4.0–4.1 mt from Lanjigarh, with H2 much higher than H1; alumina cost expected to approach USD750/t from Q2 (Q1 was USD780/t).
Group FY27 EBITDA outlook for Vedanta India on a consol basis about USD9.5–10 bn; cash conversion about 50%; group capex about INR20,000 crore; VRL deleveraging about USD2–2.5 bn.
Dividend framework: 4–5% yield on each entity's market capitalisation; VAML interim dividend INR8/share declared, first for the company.
Vedanta Limited FY27 growth capex about INR7,000 crore and maintenance capex about INR4,000 crore; VAML FY27 capex about INR5,000 crore (BALCO INR2,000–2,500 crore), FY28 about INR3,500–4,000 crore.
Vedanta Power plans 4.8 GW by FY27-end from 4.2 GW, with a further 7.2 GW from FY30 onwards; Sakti Unit 1 restart end-Sep/early-Oct, Unit 2 completion by end of calendar year.
capex_capacity: VAML: Sijimali bauxite mine awaiting consent to operate, targeted to start after monsoon with 1–2 mt this year and 6–7 mt next year; Kuraloi coal mine to yield up to 2 mt this FY and 8 mt next year.
BALCO Potline 3: produced 24 kt in Q1 vs plan of 22 kt; FY27 volume about 260–270 kt; full run-rate exit this year, FY28 total 435 kt from expansion.
Vedanta Power: Sakti Unit 1 restart by end-Sep/early-Oct and completion by Q4 FY27; Unit 2 completion targeted by end of calendar 2026; Meenakshi moving to 100% domestic coal.
VISL: Bokaro expansion Stage 1 forest clearance received; Stage 2 expected by end of Q2; expansion targeted by end of FY27; Goa ductile iron pipe project later this year.
Vedanta Limited: Gamsberg Phase 2 starting August, adding 200 kt MIC capacity to 450 ktpa; Copper India capacity 222 ktpa with debottlenecking to 229 ktpa; Zinc India smelter expansion by Q2 FY29.
demand_pricing: Brent prices up about 15% QoQ supported Vedanta Oil & Gas EBITDA; sales volume about 85% of production, with the quarter's stock build sold post-monsoon.
Global aluminium prices buoyant on supply constraints; Q1 hedges were 293 kt at USD2,813/t; Q2 hedge 270 kt at USD2,830/t; 28% of remaining volumes hedged at USD3,062/t average.
Power: India hit all-time high demand of 271 GW in May 2026; import coal prices up over 60%, but Meenakshi contained coal cost up only 12% YoY by using 65–70% Indian coal.
Copper International rod sales down 51% YoY due to Middle East supply disruption; ferrochrome ore production at FACOR up 41% YoY to 153 kt.
Alumina bought-out vs captive gap estimated at USD50–60/t at current API; domestic bauxite cost near USD300/t alumina cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can the VAML alumina output of about 4.1 mt be achieved given the run-rate of roughly 1.1 mt per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon months are weaker, so volumes will be H2-heavy, and it reiterated the 4.0–4.1 mt Lanjigarh guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected debt levels and capex for VAML, and when will the next expansion start?
qa_highlights.answer: VAML net debt is about INR29,500 crore; remaining growth capex is INR7,000–8,000 crore over 18–24 months. The 3 mtpa expansion is still on the drawing board, with details to come in about a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Vedanta group dividend policy after the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy moved from prescriptive to descriptive for each entity, with the group targeting a 4–5% yield on each company's market cap; VAML may fund about half of group dividends.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on VRL debt and funding needs?
qa_highlights.answer: VRL debt is about USD5 bn; about USD0.4 bn is needed for the rest of FY27, largely via dividends. FY28 needs about USD1 bn, including a USD1 bn bridge loan to be refinanced, and the brand fee is fixed to March 2029.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Vedanta Oil & Gas revenue flat QoQ despite Brent up about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales are cyclical, with about 85% of volumes sold, and the remaining stock is liquidated post-monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Sijimali mining and what approvals remain?
qa_highlights.answer: Only consent to operate is pending, expected this quarter; mining would start after the monsoon, with an MDO partner already appointed.

risks_watch: Sakti Unit 1 restart slipped from earlier timing to end-September/early-October; Vedanta Power Q1 EBITDA of INR291 crore and a INR487 crore exceptional item hit PAT, so restart timing is a key watch item.
VAML alumina output must reach 4.0–4.1 mt, but Q1 was about 826 kt and management says H2 must be much higher than H1; monsoon power-plant shutdowns may push Q2 hot metal cost marginally higher.

Sijimali bauxite mine depends on consent to operate, with management expecting it this quarter and mining after monsoon; Sumangal's question on starting production by Q4 got only a qualitative 'hopeful' answer.
Management declined to quantify procurement from OMC, saying the matter is sub judice, which limits visibility into bauxite cost economics.
Vedanta Resources refinancing: VRL debt about USD5 bn, FY28 needs about USD1 bn including a USD1 bn bridge loan to be refinanced; dividends from subsidiaries are the main funding source.
Vedanta Oil & Gas natural decline and flat QoQ revenue despite Brent up about 15-30%; unit opex guided flat to FY26 and reported PAT includes a INR1,097 crore discontinued-ops gain.
Pending upgrade of India Ratings, which management said could come within weeks, and the 3 mtpa VAML expansion, still on drawing board with details due in about a quarter.
Zinc International volume ramp toward 300 kt and cost guidance; management said any cost guidance revision would come in H2, not now.
key_quotes: So, the way to look at, Indrajit, I mean, if you look at historically, Vedanta's dividend yield has been quite high, in fact, double digit, 12%, 13%.
Yes. So as regards BALCO ramp-up is concerned, against a plan of 22 kt in Q1, BALCO produced 24 kt from the new potline.
Ritesh, you are aware that this matter is sub judice, that is where I did not want to indicate the number because you are aware that we are getting this under the court order as of now.
So, it is only a question of time.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on headline results, VAML cost and balance-sheet deleveraging, and firm on the Sijimali and Sakti timelines. It was guarded or evasive on the 3 mtpa expansion details, the OMC bauxite procurement numbers (sub judice), and Zinc International FY27 cost guidance, deferring those to later updates.

adds.what: Vedanta Power 4.2 GW to 4.8 GW by FY27-end (Sakti Unit 1 restart and Unit 2 completion)
Gamsberg Phase 2 adding 200 kt MIC capacity to 450 ktpa (Vedanta Limited)
BALCO Potline 3 ramp to full run-rate, FY28 total 435 kt from expansion
Sijimali bauxite mine 1-2 mt this year, 6-7 mt next year, awaiting consent to operate

growth.why: Q1 FY27 VAML revenue +45% YoY and EBITDA +134% YoY on record 632 kt output and higher realisations; FY27 hot metal cost guided unchanged at USD1,650-1,700/t and Lanjigarh alumina 4.0-4.1 mt with H2 weighted, backed by Potline 3 ramp, Sijimali/Kuraloi mines and Power capacity additions, but no firm group revenue growth number was guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: VAML EBITDA per ton rose to USD1,804 from USD1,511 QoQ and hot metal cost is guided at USD1,650-1,700/t, with a further USD175-200/t reduction over 3-4 quarters from Lanjigarh, Sijimali and Ghogharpalli, though Q2 cost may tick up on monsoon power shutdowns and alumina cost is guided to approach USD750/t from Q2 (Q1 USD780/t).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Lanjigarh alumina to 4.0-4.1 mt in FY27 (H2-heavy from Q1 run-rate about 1.1 mt per quarter), BALCO Potline 3 full run-rate exit this year with FY27 volume 260-270 kt, Sijimali consent expected this quarter with mining after monsoon, and Vedanta Power 4.2 GW to 4.8 GW by FY27-end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: VAML alumina output must rise from 826 kt in Q1 to hit 4.0-4.1 mt, and Sijimali adds 1-2 mt this year and 6-7 mt next year; Q1 aluminium was a record 632 kt (+5% YoY) and value-added products 389 kt (+14% YoY).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: VAML guides FY27 capex about INR5,000 crore and FY28 INR3,500-4,000 crore, with a 3 mtpa expansion details due in about a quarter and remaining growth capex INR7,000-8,000 crore over 18-24 months; group capex about INR20,000 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: VAML guidance held (hot metal USD1,650-1,700/t, alumina 4.0-4.1 mt) despite Q1 EBITDA per ton of USD1,804 and buoyant aluminium prices with Q2 hedges at USD2,830/t; management did not raise numbers and Zinc cost guidance is deferred to H2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Alumina needs H2 far above H1 to reach 4.0-4.1 mt, Sakti Unit 1 restart slipped to end-Sep/early-Oct, and Q2 hot metal cost may rise marginally on monsoon shutdowns; Oil & Gas revenue flat QoQ despite Brent up about 15-30%.

rows.label: Sakti Unit 1 restart
rows.why: Vedanta Power Q1 EBITDA fell to INR291 crore after the Sakti boiler incident and INR487 crore exceptional item; restart guided end-Sep/early-Oct with completion by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: VRL deleveraging and dividend flow
rows.why: VRL debt about USD5 bn with about USD0.4 bn needed for rest of FY27 mainly via subsidiary dividends, and VAML net debt/EBITDA down to 0.9x from 1.3x while VAML pays first INR8/share interim dividend.

rows.label: Sijimali bauxite mine start
rows.why: Only consent to operate pending (expected this quarter); mine targets 1-2 mt this year and 6-7 mt next year, with MDO partner already appointed.

tone.note: Management was confident on record VAML results, the hot metal cost guidance and deleveraging, and firm on Sijimali and Sakti timelines; it was guarded on the 3 mtpa expansion details, OMC bauxite procurement (sub judice) and Zinc International cost guidance, and analysts pressed on alumina H2 ramp
